decisions.reason: The two triples (1,1,1) and (1,2,1/2) give the same s=2, manifold, metric and orientation but retain different G_N and m_*. Thus the claimed equivalence of parameterized and geometric data was false. Clause (c) now retains the parameterized quadruple and identifies (M,g,N) only as its associated geometric datum, dependent on s alone; the metric, domains, fields and hypotheses are unchanged.

For s=c=1 the listed energy e=2sqrt(2)/3 is irrational, and several other listed quantities involve c^2*s^2 or c^2/s^2 rather than the stated unit factors. This was a false expository arithmetic description, not a failure of the exact evaluated formulas. Replaced it with exact-evaluation wording and identified the irrational factor. Checked the substitutions at 3s, 3s/2 and 4s, fixed-ell differentiation and threshold divergence; L1 now faithfully distinguishes constructed equatorial quantities from orientation-independent nonexistence, and proof 2.1 uses the supplier clause (b) for every orientation.

Longitude speed is not invariant under rotations: a meridional circular geodesic has locally constant longitude, while G_N*m_*/r_0^3 is positive. Repaired (c)(1) without restricting angular orientation: for sigma=iota composed with gamma and t=x^0/c, define Omega^2=gamma_S2(sigma_prime,sigma_prime)/(t_prime)^2. The supplier circular-orbit lemma proof 2.2 derives the radial identity in arbitrary angular charts. Future timelikeness gives t_prime>0, so dividing gives Omega^2=c^2*f_prime/(2r_0)=G_N*m_*/r_0^3. At the equator this equals squared longitude speed. Checked vacuum admissibility, clock normalization and nonzero interval, isotropic leading coefficient and adopted comparison conventions; no measured input or empirical inference is introduced.

The consulted Minguzzi PDF identifies section 4.1 as reflectivity and the transverse ladder and section 4.2 as the lower causal-ladder levels, not the attributed event horizons/trapped sets. This is a nonfatal bibliographic error: the local horizon conclusions have explicit suppliers. Replaced the title with the actually read section 1 opening, printed p. 3, on spacetime/causal-cone conventions and C^2 curvature regularity.
